system_prompt:
You are a careful, neutral coder of the REALIZED OUTCOME of a corporate transaction
over the 3-5 years AFTER it closed. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from
public primary sources (financial filings, reputable press) that describes ONLY the
post-deal trajectory -- how the combined company actually fared. You are
DELIBERATELY NOT shown how the deal was structured at closing (what transferred and
what did not), and you must NOT speculate about the deal's structure. Code STRICTLY
the documented realized outcome. If the slice does not let you determine a field,
you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from outside knowledge.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

C. FAILURE-PATHWAY INCIDENCE -- code strictly from the DOCUMENTED OUTCOME at the
3-5 year horizon. A pathway is a REALIZED DISRUPTION OVER TIME, not a structural
property of the deal.
  p4_pathway: Is there documented disruption specifically at the product/process
    interface (the acquired product could not be aligned with the operating
    processes over time; product-line/operations incoherence realized after the
    deal)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented; uncertain.
  p5_pathway: Is there documented fracture specifically at the process/organization
    interface (operations vs people/management/culture; integration of operations
    broke against the organization over time)? 1 = yes; 0 = no / none documented;
    uncertain.
  t1_archetype: Is there documented incoherence in the controlling-intent archetype
    itself as it played out (e.g. an announced "merger of equals" that operated as
    one-sided dominance)? A channel SEPARATE from the product/process and
    process/organization pathways. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  t2_model: Is there documented incompatibility of the two business models
    (value-capture logics that could not be reconciled over time)? A channel
    SEPARATE from the pathways above. 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.

D. performance_metric: the single best-documented post-deal outcome scalar in the
   slice (e.g. "divested 80.1% after ~108 months", "~$99bn goodwill write-down",
   "no divestiture; assets retained"). One short phrase. If none, "not documented".

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your p4_pathway and
p5_pathway codes specifically. Cite ONLY realized-outcome evidence; do NOT reason
about how the deal was structured at closing.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: absence of documented
evidence for a pathway is 0 (not-documented); inability to determine is "uncertain".

# Outcome sub-dossier — acquired RadioShack business under General Wireless, realized record ~2015-2020

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. The business acquired in the 2015 sale was held by
> a privately owned buyer (General Wireless) that files no SEC periodic reports, so the
> realized record is traced through court records and reputable press. This sub-dossier
> contains no information about how the transaction was structured at closing.

## Public-reporting status of the acquired business (feasibility-relevant)
- The buyer, General Wireless Inc. / General Wireless Operations Inc. (doing business as
  RadioShack), is privately held and files no annual reports or other periodic reports on
  EDGAR; consequently no audited public financial statements exist for the acquired
  business, and the realized-record facts below rely on court records and reputable press.
  [UNVERIFIED]

## Realized record — second Chapter 11 filing
- On March 8, 2017, General Wireless Operations Inc. dba RadioShack and affiliated debtors
  filed a voluntary petition for relief under chapter 11 in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for
  the District of Delaware, assigned Case No. 17-10506 — the second Chapter 11 filing for
  the RadioShack brand within roughly two years. [SRC: https://www.abi.org/feed-item/new-delaware-chapter-11-filing-%E2%80%93-general-wireless-operations-inc-dba-radioshack-%E2%80%93-case-no]
- Reputable press reported the filing on March 9, 2017: "General Wireless Operations Inc.,
  doing business as electronics convenience store RadioShack," announced it had filed for
  Chapter 11 protection. [SRC: https://www.retaildive.com/news/radioshack-files-for-second-bankruptcy-in-24-months-closing-200-stores/437752/]

## Realized record — documented disruption over time
- The court filing indicated that while the core RadioShack retail business had returned
  to profitability, the partnership with Sprint Solutions Inc. did not succeed and left
  the debtors with inadequate capital to continue as a going concern; the cases were
  filed to close additional underperforming stores and to pursue a sale or restructuring.
  [SRC: https://www.abi.org/feed-item/new-delaware-chapter-11-filing-%E2%80%93-general-wireless-operations-inc-dba-radioshack-%E2%80%93-case-no]
- Approximately 200 RadioShack stores were to close, with options being evaluated on the
  remaining approximately 1,300 locations; press reported Sprint "helps run about a third
  of its brick-and-mortar operations in co-branded stores." [SRC: https://www.retaildive.com/news/radioshack-files-for-second-bankruptcy-in-24-months-closing-200-stores/437752/]

## Realized record — disposition of the brand
- On November 19, 2020, Retail Ecommerce Ventures (REV) acquired the RadioShack brands and
  related assets, including RadioShack.com and related websites across the U.S., Canada,
  India, Australia, Europe and China; the prior owner, General Wireless Operations,
  retained a minority stake, and the deal terms were not disclosed. [SRC: https://www.retaildive.com/news/radioshack-brand-acquired-by-new-owner-of-pier-1-modells-ip/589377/]

## Items noted but not primary-verifiable
- Third-party accounts describe the remaining RadioShack footprint at the time of the 2020
  brand sale (e.g., a few hundred independent authorized dealers, HobbyTown-affiliated
  outlets, and an online operation), but these counts are not traceable to a retrieved
  primary court filing or SEC document and are recorded here as [UNVERIFIED]. [UNVERIFIED]

## Outcome summary (realized record only)
- The acquired RadioShack retail business, held by a privately owned buyer that files no
  SEC reports, re-entered Chapter 11 on March 8, 2017 (Case No. 17-10506) — approximately
  two years after the 2015 sale — with roughly 200 stores set to close and about 1,300
  evaluated, the filing attributing the shortfall to a co-branding partnership with Sprint
  that did not succeed and left inadequate capital; the RadioShack brand and related web
  assets were subsequently sold to Retail Ecommerce Ventures on November 19, 2020, with
  the prior owner retaining a minority stake. [SRC: https://www.abi.org/feed-item/new-delaware-chapter-11-filing-%E2%80%93-general-wireless-operations-inc-dba-radioshack-%E2%80%93-case-no] [SRC: https://www.retaildive.com/news/radioshack-files-for-second-bankruptcy-in-24-months-closing-200-stores/437752/] [SRC: https://www.retaildive.com/news/radioshack-brand-acquired-by-new-owner-of-pier-1-modells-ip/589377/]

[SLICE END]

There is no documented evidence of disruption specifically at the product/process interface (p4_pathway) or the process/organization interface (p5_pathway)."
